description: Decision layers settled with the user before expensive work (studio/decisions.py). Each layer body is closed: an edit to a path the schema does not define is refused.

place.description: where the story happens, in words (decided before the camera); generate backdrop-review --shot uses it when no --place is given

about.description: what the claim is about, so what a line that says it must show: a world element id, a subject id, subject/part_id or subject/feature_id (a spec feature: any of its parts). [] when it explains nothing that can be seen (studio/explains.py)

story.description: The story before the script (studio/story_core.py): beats with a dramatic function, how tense each is and its share of the reel. The script's lines name their beat; the shots follow the beats.

direction.description: the axis values a story drawn before 2026-10-20 was drawn from (library/story_axes.json); stories since grow from a judged pitch (pitch)

thread.description: the drawn thread kind (library/story_axes.json thread); stories drawn before 2026-10-19 have none

stake.description: the drawn stake kind (library/story_axes.json stake); stories drawn before 2026-10-20 have none

pitch.description: the judged pitch this story grew from (studio/story_pitch.py; story add checks it is the slot's - STORY_PITCH_DIFFERS)

line.description: the pitch in one line: its opening and question

stake.description: what the viewer has at risk in how it turns out (story_core.stake_lint): whose, what; the story comes back to it at its end

who.description: whose it is: the viewer, a rider, a city, the crew

what_is_at_risk.description: what is lost if it goes wrong (or won, if it goes right), in words

closed_by.description: the beat that comes back to the stake - the last one (STAKE_NOT_CLOSED)

thread.description: the one thing the viewer keeps hold of from beat to beat (story_core.chain_lint): its kind orders the beats; the carrier stays on screen (reel_flow THREAD_OFF_SCREEN)

kind.description: a value of library/story_axes.json thread (moving, time, question, change, failure, scale, ...)

carrier.description: what is on screen that carries it, in words (the water, the chain link, the building)

carrier_ids.description: the world elements or subject/part ids that carry it on screen; a shot shows one of them (shots name what they show)

why_watch.description: what keeps the viewer watching through this beat

picture_idea.description: the picture that carries the beat, in words

link.description: how this beat follows the one before: so - because of it; but - against it (a doubt, a complication, what goes wrong); and - merely after it (a list). Not on the first beat

raises.description: the question the viewer is left with after this beat (the hook's is the reel's question)

answers.description: the earlier beats whose question (raises) this beat answers

on_screen.description: what happens on screen in this beat - an event the viewer sees, not a line they hear (HOOK_UNSEEN, TURN_SPOKEN_ONLY)

event.description: the event as seen: what moves, breaks, appears or changes (not a question, not a quote)

kind.description: contradiction - a belief broken; failure - something goes wrong; payoff_first - the result shown first; anomaly - something odd happens; change - a state turns into another

returns_to.description: the earlier beat whose picture this one comes back to - the last beat to the hook (CLOSE_NOT_RETURNING)

story_beat_id.description: the story beat this line belongs to (the story layer); required once the project's ladder has a story

role.description: the shot's job on screen (references/screen_grammar.md 4.G); it chooses the pattern section the shot reads (studio pattern show). detail/outro/transition are older names (explain/close/none)

line_ids.description: the script lines said over this shot, in order. A line said across a cut is in each shot it runs through: the last line of the shot it starts in, the first (at 0) of the next ones (decisions.span_lines) - the voice runs on, the picture changes

frame.description: the cut's screen, decided before any picture: what it holds in focus (world element, subject, subject/part ids) and how large that focus stands in the frame - what studio/maker.py reads to decide who makes the cut

size.description: wide: the place around it reads; medium: the thing whole, filling much of the frame; close: part of it fills the frame; detail: one part fills it

kind.description: mechanism: the cut shows how the thing works (a working part in focus, the key change, an opening); world: the place, people, a result, a scale, a comparison around it - replaced 2026-10-20 by keeps: read, never used

keeps.description: read, never used since 2026-10-20 (KEEPS_NOT_READ): what must be right in a cut is what its lines say on screen (studio/maker.implied_keeps)

what.description: in words: what must be right (the ball swings against the sway)

maker.description: who makes this cut, when the shot list says so (else studio/maker.py proposes it): generative (a video model from the cut's picture), hybrid (Blender shape, the model's look) or blender. Never one that cannot keep what the cut must keep - its keeps and what its lines claim on screen (MAKER_KEEP_UNCOVERED)

pattern.description: what this shot takes from its role's patterns, carried into this project (aspect, length, subject), and what it leaves on purpose - read with studio pattern show; the departures reach shot.screen.pattern_departs

beat_ids.description: the world beats this shot tells

direction.description: How the shot is directed, in words the user reads on the sheet (2026-10-11, the user: "어떻게 역동적으로 카메라에 담고 ... 배경에는 뭘 넣을지"): the camera, what the subject does when, what sits in front, middle and back, the size against the shot before, and how it hands over to the next shot

reveal.description: How the shot shows what is inside or hidden (the screen grammar's reveal vocabulary): a section the camera pushes into, an exploded view, see-through skin... The build is measured for it (REVEAL_NOT_SHOWN); a shot list without any is held against the user's reference (REVEAL_UNPLANNED)

move.description: How the shot moves, chosen as a motion (2026-10-22): a recipe from library/camera_recipes.json (a feel), what the motion reveals, when its key moment comes (0-1 of the shot) and why for this scene. A recipe with a make is built by the engine from the scene (studio/recipe_moves.py); settings choose its values inside the recipe's ranges.

cut.description: the move's focus may run off the side edges: its height is fitted, not its width (a long thing large in a narrow frame). The director's choice with its why; default whole

items.description: a framing the camera passes through (recipe_moves.moments_move: a frame_to_frame frame); the same framing twice rests the camera

size.description: how tall what it frames stands in the frame (height share; past 1 runs off)

centre.description: [x, y] of the framed middle (default: the UI-free frame's middle)

cut.description: the framed subject runs off the top and bottom

hold.description: keep the camera where the moment before left it (a falling thing crosses a still frame); size and view are then that moment's

moments.description: the motion as framings in time order, joined by the engine (frame_to_frame): approach, rest, turn round; a recipe without an engine make is written so

path.description: how moments are joined (auto: round the subject when they look from different sides)

follow.description: how much of the subject's travel the camera shares between moments

items.description: a framing the camera passes through (recipe_moves.moments_move: a frame_to_frame frame); the same framing twice rests the camera

size.description: how tall what it frames stands in the frame (height share; past 1 runs off)

centre.description: [x, y] of the framed middle (default: the UI-free frame's middle)

cut.description: the framed subject runs off the top and bottom

hold.description: keep the camera where the moment before left it (a falling thing crosses a still frame); size and view are then that moment's

moments.description: the motion as framings in time order, joined by the engine (frame_to_frame): approach, rest, turn round; a recipe without an engine make is written so

path.description: how moments are joined (auto: round the subject when they look from different sides)

follow.description: how much of the subject's travel the camera shares between moments

cut.description: the move's focus may run off the side edges: its height is fitted, not its width (a long thing large in a narrow frame). The director's choice with its why; default whole

others.description: the director's compared takes, made before the engine's (each framed as written)

change.description: What the shot's lines explain, happening on screen (2026-10-22): each change - its parts, its kind (library/change_kinds.json), from and to in the kind's units, when within the shot, why. The build makes it (blender_ops/change_scene.py) and measures the screen between its start and end (studio/change_moves.py).

axis.description: the world's x, y or z, or the object's own height (nearest the world's up), length and width

still.description: Why the shot holds with nothing changing on screen (when it has no change)

at.description: the moment: the start, the end, or a share of the shot (a key picture)

parts.description: what this moment must show: part ids of a subject spec, or world element ids

how.description: how the parts show (studio/blender_ops/show_core.SHOW_METHODS): the picture is drawn this way and the scene builds it

min_px.description: how thick each part must show, in output pixels (default: show_core.SHOW_MIN_SHARE of the height)

key.description: this moment is the explanation's key change - what turns or happens that the reel is about (a chain jumping to the next sprocket, a valve opening): the shot list of a story with a turn or climax marks one (KEY_CHANGE_UNPLANNED), and the build must show these parts large and unhidden at this moment (KEY_CHANGE_UNSHOWN; studio/reel_flow.py)

focus.description: what this moment frames (camera_moves_core.frame_target): the camera sizes and aims this moment on these ids; absent = the move's target

show.description: What each moment of the shot shows and how - decided before its pictures (2026-10-13, the user: the picture is drawn as a section from the start; the camera never hunts for an angle)

thread_to.description: the story's thread passes here to these carriers (world elements or subject/part ids): the shots after this one hold them instead (reel_flow THREAD_OFF_SCREEN) - the water hands over to the air it pushes

handover.description: How this shot hands over to the next: continue (the same subject and motion run on), match_action (one action cut in two), contrast (a deliberate change), new_place (another subject or place)

line_at_s.description: Where each of line_ids starts in the shot, in seconds (same order; the first usually 0). The time between one line's end and the next start is picture alone: a section opening, a mechanism moving (2026-10-12, the user: "훅훅 넘어가는 느낌"). Without it the lines follow each other closely.

story_beat_ids.description: the story beats this shot tells; from its lines when left out (a wordless shot names its own)

place.description: Where the shot's subjects stand (2026-10-22 r3: a stone the lines drop past the boat stood unplaced at the origin, inside the hull). Each subject the shot builds (an element with a subject spec) but one says where it stands: world metres, the main subject at the origin unless placed, rot_z_deg turning it about the world's up. The director's choice with its why; materialized into the shot's scene.instances.

cut.description: The rough cut the user watched whole, and the scene version of every shot in it; finals and paid generation render exactly these.

versions.description: filled from the cut when left out (a generative shot has no scene version)

world.description: The world the video happens in, settled from a picture of every beat before the shot list (studio/world.py): what kind of world it is, its place, light and people, and each element with who makes its shape and its look.

kind.description: continuous: one place the shots share (kept alike by a world reference picture); independent: each shot its own place; none: an explanation with no world (a stage tone and light only)

temperature_k.description: the colour of the light that leads (sun, or the lamps of a night interior)

white_balance_k.description: the camera white balance; left out, the look decides

ids.description: scene ids that build this element (its parts or stand-ins), linked once built

medium.description: a medium the viewer sees through (water a hull floats in, glass, a haze): its scene ids are drawn half see-through over every shot and block no ray, so the camera and the build see what is in it as the picture does (show_core.MEDIUM)

line_ids.description: the script lines that name this thing (a person, an organisation, another technique, a place): the shots of those lines show it (STORY_ELEMENT_UNSHOWN)

blockout.description: the element's clay stand-in at its real size (studio/world.py): the engine builds it where a shot's scene.stand_ins places it, so its place and size are decided in 3D and only its look is the model's

size_m.description: x, y, z in metres (a cylinder: diameter x, diameter y, height)

scale_ref.description: a thing of a size everyone knows (a person, a car, a bus): counts as the shot's scale reference

shell.description: the environment shell the engine builds (studio/blender_ops/env_shell_core.py): the ground or sea reaching the horizon and the sky over it, so the horizon and the sky are decided in 3D; their look is the model's

relief.description: hills round the place (env_shell_core.relief_height): a ring of rolling ground from start_m out to RELIEF_OUTER x it, rising to about height_m - the horizon line a picture of a valley, a lake or a coast draws; nothing inside start_m, where the subject stands

camera.description: where the shot's cameras stand against the ground: over it (default) or under it - water seen from inside, its surface a ceiling (env_shell_core.UNDER)
